title: Traffic Decibel Index & Release Sampling Protocol
body:
Purpose:
This working doc introduces a compact operational metric (Traffic Decibel Index, TDI) and a paired sampling protocol to standardize how we scale telemetry sampling and throttles during staged rollouts. Goal: reduce noise in post-deploy signal while retaining fidelity for regressions and user-visible degradation.

TL;DR (two lines):
- TDI = weighted sum of 5 signal channels (latency p95, error-rate spike, token-cost variance, traffic-slope, queue-depth) normalized to 0-100.
- Mapping: TDI < 15 = green (min sampling), 15-40 = amber (increase sampling to 5%), 40-70 = red (sample 20%, enable canary rollback gates), >70 = panic (full trace capture + rollback recommended).

Open questions / assumptions:
- weighting: default weights proposed below — need sign-off from SRE and Observability (Mark + Priya to confirm).
- overhead: higher sampling adds ~7% CPU in collector path (measured on staging). Acceptable?
- customer impact: what telemetry is PII-sensitive — ensure sampling never forces sending payloads that violate redwood privacy rules.

TDI calculation (proposal):
- latency_p95_score (0-100): map p95 relative to baseline (baseline = last 7d). + weight 0.30
- error_spike_score (0-100): sudden delta relative to 1h rolling baseline. + weight 0.30
- token_cost_variance (0-100): token-per-response variance normalized. + weight 0.15
- traffic_slope (0-100): derivative of request/sec over 15m window mapped to index. + weight 0.15
- queue_depth_score (0-100): worker queue length relative to soft limit. + weight 0.10

Operational mapping (what to do when TDI moves):
- Green (0-14):
  - Sampling: 1% token sampling (prefix-only), event-level aggregates only
  - Routing: no changes
  - Alerts: none beyond baseline dashboards
  - Notes: proceed canary expansion per schedule

- Amber (15-39):
  - Sampling: 5% full-request sampling, preserve KV-cache traces for 10% of samples
  - Routing: pause last expansion step (if currently at scheduled ramp)
  - Alerts: page on sustained >20 for 15m (ops lead)
  - Play: ops lead to run quick smoke (30m) and confirm no model/regression signal

- Red (40-69):
  - Sampling: 20% full-request + 100% error-path traces for 30m
  - Routing: auto-fallback to compatible model-variant (if policy exists) for 10% of traffic
  - Alerts: page SRE + model-oncall immediately
  - Play: hold further ramp, consider rollback if signals persist >30m

- Panic (70+):
  - Sampling: full trace, full logs capture (enable extended retention for debugging)
  - Routing: immediate diversion to stable region/capacity pool, throttle non-essential routes
  - Alerts: full incident response (SEV-1 semantics)
  - Play: consider automated rollback after guard-window (10m) unless confirmed cause is non-product (infra, cloud provider)

Preflight checklist (to be run 48-12h before rollout):
- [ ] confirm canary calendar in shared calendar and #release-ops pinned message (owner: release lead)
- [ ] validate baseline telemetry windows (make sure last 7d used for baseline exists)
- [ ] deploy TDI-built dashboards to release namespace (obs team)
- [ ] run sample-injection test (synthetic 5m) to verify TDI moves as expected (qa)
- [ ] confirm sampling toggles are staged and authoring permission saved (infra)
- [ ] confirm rollback tag/bundle exists in artifact registry and can be applied within 5m (release-eng)
- [ ] customer-impact check: ensure top-10 enterprise customers are notified if the rollout expands beyond 20% traffic (cs)

Rollout calendar (compact, 72h window example):
Day 0 (T-72h):
- Draft release notes (internal) posted to confluence -> link in linked artifacts
- Preflight checklist kickoff call (30m)

Day 1 (T-48h):
- Canary start: 1% traffic (12h soak) -> autosample=1%
- Nightshift owner assigned (if relevant)
- Health check: TDI check at 0h, 4h, 8h, 12h

Day 2 (T-24h):
- Ramp to 5% (if TDI stayed <15 for last 12h)
- Enable amber sampling settings, snapshot telemetry for goldens
- Midday ops quick sync (15m)

Day 3 (T-0h):
- Ramp to 25% after automated checks (canary pipeline completes)
- If TDI < 15, continue to 50% next window; otherwise hold and investigate
- Final release notes draft circulation to PM + comms

Rollout signals to gate on (quick list):
- sustained TDI > 20 for 30m
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline
- error-rate > 0.5% absolute (or relative spike > 300%)
- token-unit cost delta upward > 30% across cohort

Emergency rollback matrix (short):
- Criteria: any panic-level signal or persistent red for > 30m + customer-impact evidence
- Steps:
  1) freeze traffic expansion (release lead)
  2) trigger rollback tag in artifact registry -> apply in orchestrator (release-eng)
  3) revert routing rules to last-stable policy (sre)
  4) enable extended sampling and collect traces for 1h
  5) postmortem owner assigned in 24h (ops lead)

Post-release sampling retro (what to keep/turn off):
- After stable 72h window: gradually reduce sampling to baseline over 48h (50% -> 20% -> 5% -> baseline)
- Archive detailed traces to short-term store (30d) then move to cold archive if needed

Draft release notes (internal -> external later):
- internal title: "Small-model-routing and batching improvements — Aug 2026 canary"
- summary bullets (internal):
  - reduced upstream serialization overhead -> median latency down ~6% in staging
  - model-routing introduced lightweight fallback for overloaded capacity pools
  - batching heuristics tuned for short-sequence workloads, lowers token cost variance
- known issues (open): 
  - infrequent KV-cache miss causing ~5-10ms p95 spikes under synthetic worst-case (tracked: JIRA-RELEASE-1142)
  - observability: sampling needs calibration on large enterprise traffic patterns (action: obs team)

Notes to reviewers / next steps:
- Mark: can you validate the TDI weights and expected staging curves?
- Priya: confirm sampling impact on collector CPU + extra cost estimate
- Sofia: sanity-check the customer-comm threshold for enterprise notifications
- Liam: script the quick rollback operator (one-liner) and put it behind the release lead page
